page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 32 vCPUs, corresponding to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance is characterized by its integrated graphics acceleration, featuring four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with a combined VRAM of 64 GB. It does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23575.63 and a PassMark CPU score of 21092.78. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.89 and poor single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 118.4 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 57.05 GB/sec for writes. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of parallel GPU compute resources, though the underlying Intel Xeon Skylake architecture and Volta GPUs represent an older hardware generation compared to newer architectures.

The ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is designed for workloads that benefit from multi-GPU acceleration. Suitable use cases include machine learning model training, deep learning inference, high-performance computing simulations, and parallelized data processing tasks that can leverage the four NVIDIA V100 GPUs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for parallel computing workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance's primary capability comes from its four integrated NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, which provide a total of 64 GB of VRAM. It contains no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core CPU capabilities alongside moderate memory bandwidth, while single-core performance remains weak. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for legacy GPU-accelerated tasks, making it highly suitable for machine learning training, deep learning inference, and high-performance computing workloads that require multi-GPU configurations.
